meta.title: Microsoft Fluent 2 (Fluent UI React v9) component catalog

sources.detail: Storybook index; every docs entry has a companion LLM markdown page at https://storybooks.fluentui.dev/react/llms/<id>.txt carrying the react-docgen prop table (Name/Type/Required/Default/Description), Subcomponents, Best practices and compiling Examples.
API-Extractor report for @fluentui/react-components. Maps every re-exported symbol to the package that owns it, which is how reactImport is resolved rather than assumed.

Custom elements manifest shipped in @fluentui/web-components@3.1.0. Every fluent-* tag, its kebab-case attributes and its registration subpath are read from here; a tag that is not in the manifest is cleared rather than carried forward.

@fluentui-copilot/react-copilot@0.30.5 rollup d.ts plus each of its 32 @fluentui-copilot/* sub-package d.ts files (props and slots come from the sub-packages). ai.fluentui.dev is Entra-gated and is not a usable source; the npm tarball is public and is.
@fluentui/react-icons@2.0.337; used only to confirm the symbols the Icon record names actually exist (bundleIcon plus the sample icons).

fieldNotes: maturity: stable | preview | compat | migration | utility | deprecated. Derived from the Storybook title path (Components/ = stable, Compat Components/ = compat, Preview Components/ + Motion "(preview)" = preview, Migration Shims/ = migration, Utilities/ = utility) and corrected by the resolved package suffix (-preview / -compat). Every @fluentui-copilot/* package is 0.x, so the whole AI suite is preview.
keyProps[].required mirrors the upstream Required column verbatim (React v9) or the absence of `?` on the declared member (AI suite).
keyProps[].slot and slots[] list the slot props (types containing Slot<>/WithSlotShorthandValue<>), which the previous catalog omitted entirely.
reactImport is derived from the identifiers the sample actually uses plus the package that owns the component, so the import always covers the sample.

webComponent / webComponentDefine / webComponentAttributes come from the custom elements manifest. Attribute names are kebab-case (icon-only, disabled-focusable) and deliberately do NOT mirror the React camelCase prop names.

AI-suite records carry both imports: reactImport (umbrella, or the sub-package when the umbrella does not re-export the component) and reactImportTreeShakable (always the sub-package). umbrellaExport:false means importing from @fluentui-copilot/react-copilot will NOT resolve.

Docgen strips props inherited from native HTML elements (disabled, placeholder, min/max/step). Their absence from keyProps is a limitation of the source table, not a statement that the prop does not exist - the samples show them in use.
verified: true means the record was read from the sources above at generatedAt. verified: false means no public source could confirm or refute it; see verificationNote.

unmappedTags.reason: No React v9 counterpart (React composes this with an existing component).
DialogBody is exported by @fluentui/react-components but the Storybook does not document it, so there is no record to attach the tag to.

webComponents.unmappedNote: Registered tags with no record to attach to. Each entry says whether a React v9 export of that name exists (the Storybook simply never documented it) or whether React composes the behaviour differently - fluent-anchor-button is the anchor variant of Button, which React writes as <Button as="a">.
webComponents.registration: v3 registers nothing by default. Import the element you use, e.g. import '@fluentui/web-components/textarea/define.js'; - see each record's webComponentDefine.

deprecated.name: LatencyCancel
deprecated.useInstead: use the isLoading prop of CopilotMessage instead Deprecated on 07/22/2024

aiSuite.support: Every @fluentui-copilot/* package is 0.x and its README states "For internal use only. External use is not supported at this time." Published publicly and installable, but treat as an internal preview surface: APIs can change without notice.
aiSuite.docsAccess: https://ai.fluentui.dev returns 401 and redirects to an Entra-gated app, so it is not a usable source. The API facts here come from the public npm tarball instead.

retired.reason: Suggestions is the AI site pattern name, not an export. The real exports are Suggestion and SuggestionList, from @fluentui-copilot/react-suggestions.
Sensitivity is the AI site pattern name, not an export. The real exports are SensitivityLabel, SensitivityIcon and SensitivityTooltip, from @fluentui-copilot/react-sensitivity-label.

unverified.reason: None. Every record in this catalog was read from a public source at generatedAt.

skippedPages: Components/Text/Presets (subcomponent heading with no matching export)
Fluent Motion System (no matching export named "FluentMotionSystem")
Motion/Using motion slots (no matching export named "Usingmotionslots")
Motion/Using motion slots/Components with motion slots (no matching export named "Componentswithmotionslots")
notes: All components must be rendered inside a <FluentProvider theme={...}> to receive tokens.
webComponent is the Fluent Web Components v3 custom-element tag when one exists; null means the manifest registers no tag for this component (use the React component).

Records are keyed by `id` (the Storybook docs id, "<page>#<Subcomponent>", or "copilot-<name>"). `name` is the real export name and is NOT unique - see nameCollision (e.g. Components/List vs Migration Shims/V0/List, and the AI-suite Attachment and Textarea vs their v9 namesakes).

components.name: Avatar
components.description: An Avatar is a graphical representation of a user, team, or entity.

keyProps.name: image
keyProps.description: The Avatar's image. Usage e.g.: `image={{ src: '...' }}`

keyProps.name: icon
keyProps.default: `PersonRegular` (the default icon's size depends on the Avatar's size)
keyProps.description: Icon to be displayed when the avatar doesn't have an image or initials.

keyProps.name: initials
keyProps.description: (optional) Custom initials. It is usually not necessary to specify custom initials; by default they will be derived from the `name` prop, using the `getInitials` function. The initials are displayed when there is no image (including while the image is loading).

keyProps.name: badge
keyProps.type: WithSlotShorthandValue<Omit<ComponentProps<Pick<BadgeSlots, "root" | "icon">>, "color"> & Pick<BadgeProps, "size"> & { status?: PresenceBadgeStatus; outOfOffice?: boolean; } & RefAttributes<...>> | null | undefined
keyProps.description: Badge to show the avatar's presence status.

keyProps.name: active
keyProps.description: Optional activity indicator * active: the avatar will be decorated according to activeAppearance * inactive: the avatar will be reduced in size and partially transparent * unset: normal display

keyProps.name: activeAppearance
keyProps.description: The appearance when `active="active"`

keyProps.name: color
keyProps.description: The color when displaying either an icon or initials. * neutral (default): gray * brand: color from the brand palette * colorful: picks a color from a set of pre-defined colors, based on a hash of the name (or idForColor if provided) * [AvatarNamedColor]: a specific color from the theme

keyProps.name: idForColor
keyProps.description: Specify a string to be used instead of the name, to determine which color to use when color="colorful". Use this when a name is not available, but there is another unique identifier that can be used instead.

keyProps.name: name
keyProps.description: The name of the person or entity represented by this Avatar. This should always be provided if it is available. The name is used to determine the initials displayed when there is no image. It is also provided to accessibility tools.

keyProps.name: shape
keyProps.description: The avatar can have a circular or square shape.

keyProps.name: size
keyProps.description: Size of the avatar in pixels. Size is restricted to a limited set of supported values recommended for most uses (see `AvatarSizeValue`) and based on design guidelines for the Avatar control. Note: At size 16, if initials are displayed, only the first initial will be rendered. If a non-supported size is needed, set `size` to the next-smaller supported size, and set `width` and `height` to override the rendered size. For example, to set the avatar to 45px in size: `<Avatar size={40} style={{ width: '45px', height: '45px' }} />`

components.a11y: Give a name so initials and an accessible label are generated; sizes are fixed pixel values (16–128).
components.sample: <Avatar aria-label="Guest" {...props} />

components.name: AvatarGroup
components.description: An AvatarGroup is a graphical representation of multiple people associated with a given entity. AvatarGroup leverages the Avatar component, with each Avatar representing a person and containing their image, initials, or an icon. An AvatarGroup can be represented in a spread, stack, or pie layout.

keyProps.name: layout
keyProps.description: Layout the AvatarGroupItems should be displayed as.

keyProps.name: size
keyProps.description: Size of the AvatarGroupItems.

components.a11y: Use AvatarGroupItem for each person and AvatarGroupPopover for overflow via partitionAvatarGroupItems.

do: Use `partitionAvatarGroupItems` when possible.
Display all items, including inline `AvatarGroupItems`, inside `AvatarGroupPopover` when using a `pie` layout.
Use the last `AvatarGroupItems` in the `AvatarGroup` as the inline items when using a `spread` or `stack` layout.
dont: Use more than 3 `AvatarGroupItems` inside an `AvatarGroup` with `pie` layout.

components.sample:
<AvatarGroup {...props}>
  {inlineItems.map((name) => (
    <AvatarGroupItem name={name} key={name} />
  ))}
  {overflowItems && (
    <AvatarGroupPopover>
      {overflowItems.map((name) => (
        <AvatarGroupItem name={name} key={name} />
      ))}
    </AvatarGroupPopover>
  )}
</AvatarGroup>

components.description: The AvatarGroupPopover component provides a button with a Popover containing the children provided.

keyProps.name: size
keyProps.description: Determines popover padding and arrow size

keyProps.description: Tooltip shown when triggerButton is hovered.

keyProps.description: Popovers are rendered out of DOM order on `document.body` by default, use this to render the popover in DOM order

keyProps.name: appearance
keyProps.description: A popover can appear styled with brand or inverted. When not specified, the default style is used.

keyProps.type: HTMLElement | { element?: HTMLElement | null; className?: string; } | null | undefined
keyProps.default: a new element on document.body without any styling
keyProps.description: Where the portal children are mounted on DOM

keyProps.name: surfaceMotion
keyProps.description: Slot for the surface motion animation. For more information refer to the [Motion docs page](https://react.fluentui.dev/?path=/docs/motion-motion-slot--docs).

keyProps.description: Call back when the component requests to change value The `open` value is used as a hint when directly controlling the component

keyProps.name: inertTrapFocus
keyProps.description: Enables standard behavior according to the [HTML dialog spec](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLDialogElement/showModal) where the focus trap involves setting outside elements inert, making navigation leak from the trapped area back to the browser toolbar and vice-versa.

keyProps.name: open
keyProps.description: Controls the opening of the Popover

keyProps.name: defaultOpen
keyProps.description: Used to set the initial open state of the Popover in uncontrolled mode

keyProps.name: triggerButton
keyProps.description: Button that triggers the Popover.

keyProps.name: popoverSurface
keyProps.description: PopoverSurface that contains the content.

keyProps.name: closeOnScroll
keyProps.description: Close when scroll outside of it

keyProps.name: mouseLeaveDelay
keyProps.description: Sets the delay for closing popover on mouse leave

keyProps.name: withArrow
keyProps.description: Display an arrow pointing to the target.

keyProps.name: openOnContext
keyProps.description: Flag to open the Popover as a context menu. Disables all other interactions

keyProps.name: openOnHover
keyProps.description: Flag to open the Popover by hovering the trigger

keyProps.name: closeOnIframeFocus
keyProps.description: Flag to close the Popover when an iframe outside a PopoverSurface is focused

keyProps.name: positioning
keyProps.description: Configures the position of the Popover. Explore [Positioning docs](https://react.fluentui.dev/?path=/docs/concepts-developer-positioning-components--docs) for more options.

keyProps.name: trapFocus
keyProps.description: Should trap focus

keyProps.name: legacyTrapFocus
keyProps.description: Must be used with the `trapFocus` prop Enables older Fluent UI focus trap behavior where the user cannot tab into the window outside of the document. This is now non-standard behavior according to the [HTML dialog spec](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLDialogElement/showModal) where the focus trap involves setting outside elements inert.
keyProps.deprecated: this behavior is default provided now, to opt-out of it in favor of standard behavior use the `inertTrapFocus` property

keyProps.name: unstable_disableAutoFocus
keyProps.description: By default Popover focuses the first focusable element in PopoverSurface on open. Specify `disableAutoFocus` to prevent this behavior.

keyProps.name: indicator
keyProps.description: Whether the triggerButton should render an icon instead of the number of overflowed AvatarGroupItems. Note: The indicator will default to `icon` when the size is less than 24.

keyProps.name: count
keyProps.description: Number of AvatarGroupItems that will be rendered. Note: AvatarGroupPopover handles counting the number of children, but when using a react fragment to wrap the children, this is not possible and therefore it has do be added manually.

components.name: Breadcrumb
components.description: For detailed guidance on when and how to use this component, go to Fluent 2 Breadcrumbs.
components.reactImport:
import { Breadcrumb, BreadcrumbButton, BreadcrumbDivider, BreadcrumbItem } from '@fluentui/react-components';
import { CalendarMonthFilled, CalendarMonthRegular, bundleIcon } from '@fluentui/react-icons';

keyProps.name: list
keyProps.description: Ordered list which contains items.

keyProps.name: focusMode
keyProps.description: Sets the focus behavior for the Breadcrumb. `tab` This behaviour will cycle through all elements inside of the Breadcrumb when pressing the Tab key and then release focus after the last inner element. `arrow` This behaviour will cycle through all elements inside of the Breadcrumb when pressing the Arrow key.

keyProps.name: size
keyProps.description: Controls size of Breadcrumb items and dividers.

components.a11y: Renders a <nav> with an ordered list; add aria-label="Breadcrumb". Compose BreadcrumbItem/BreadcrumbButton/BreadcrumbDivider.
components.sample:
const CalendarMonth = bundleIcon(CalendarMonthFilled, CalendarMonthRegular);

<Breadcrumb aria-label="Breadcrumb default example">
  <BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbButton href={path}>Item 1</BreadcrumbButton>
  </BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbDivider />
  <BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbButton href={path} icon={<CalendarMonth />}>
      Item 2
    </BreadcrumbButton>
  </BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbDivider />
  <BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbButton href={path}>Item 3</BreadcrumbButton>
  </BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbDivider />
  <BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbButton href={path} current>
      Item 4
    </BreadcrumbButton>
  </BreadcrumbItem>
</Breadcrumb>

Give each CarouselNavButton an aria-label.

do: Limit cards to a max width of 100% of screen size.

Keep cards a uniform size where possible.
Set CarouselCards to focusMode='tab-exit' when there is multiple cards in view
Avoid focus on CarouselCards if they are a full size banner, out of view cards will be set to 'inert'.
Set an event listener on CarouselCards with EMBLA_VISIBILITY_EVENT to update state based on visibility (or use an intersectionObserver).
dont: Use percentage based widths unless also using resize breakpoints to define number of cards, i.e. a 400px window should have max 1-2 cards while a 1000px window could fit 2-4+
Set groupSize unless it is a constant set value, i.e. groupSize 2 if the size of cards is set to 50%.
Set autoplay to true unless user interacts or an action is taken (i.e. clicking autoplay button).

do: Ensure each component has clear, concise labels to help users understand their functions.
Update the display of the selected color in real-time as users interact with the sliders or input fields to provide immediate feedback.
Implement input validation for HEX and RGB text fields to ensure users enter valid formats. Provide clear error messages for invalid entries.
Allow Keyboard Input.
Ensure that color selections can be made and visualized without reliance on color alone. Use labels, indicators, and tooltips to assist users with visual impairments.
dont: Ensure consistency in color formats used throughout the ColorPicker. Avoid confusing users by mixing different formats without clear explanation.

do: Consider using `Combobox` with outline or underline appearances. When the contrast ratio against the immediate surrounding color is less than 3:1, consider using underline or outline styles which has a bottom border stroke. But please ensure the color of bottom border stroke has a sufficient contrast which is greater than 3 to 1 against the immediate surrounding color.
dont: Don’t place input on a surface which doesn’t have a sufficient contrast. The colors adjacent to the input should have a sufficient contrast. Particularly, the color of input with filled darker and lighter styles needs to provide greater than 3 to 1 contrast ratio against the immediate surrounding color to pass accessibility requirements.

components.name: Dialog
components.description: `Dialog` is a window overlaid on either the primary window or another dialog window. Windows under a modal dialog are inert. That is, users cannot interact with content outside an active dialog window. Inert content outside an active dialog is typically visually obscured or dimmed so it is difficult to discern, and in some implementations, attempts to interact with the inert content cause the dialog to close.
components.reactImport: import { Button, Dialog, DialogActions, DialogBody, DialogContent, DialogSurface, DialogTitle, DialogTrigger } from '@fluentui/react-components';

keyProps.name: surfaceMotion
keyProps.description: For more information refer to the [Motion docs page](https://react.fluentui.dev/?path=/docs/motion-motion-slot--docs).

keyProps.name: modalType
keyProps.description: Dialog variations. `modal`: When this type of dialog is open, the rest of the page is dimmed out and cannot be interacted with. The tab sequence is kept within the dialog and moving the focus outside the dialog will imply closing it. This is the default type of the component. `non-modal`: When a non-modal dialog is open, the rest of the page is not dimmed out and users can interact with the rest of the page. This also implies that the tab focus can move outside the dialog when it reaches the last focusable element. `alert`: is a special type of modal dialogs that interrupts the user's workflow to communicate an important message or ask for a decision. Unlike a typical modal dialog, the user must take an action through the options given to dismiss the dialog, and it cannot be dismissed through the dimmed background.

keyProps.name: open
keyProps.description: Controls the open state of the dialog

keyProps.name: defaultOpen
keyProps.description: Default value for the uncontrolled open state of the dialog.

keyProps.name: onOpenChange
keyProps.description: Callback fired when the component changes value from open state. @param event - a React's Synthetic event or a KeyboardEvent in case of `documentEscapeKeyDown` @param data - A data object with relevant information, such as open value and type of interaction that created the event

keyProps.name: inertTrapFocus
keyProps.description: Enables standard behavior according to the [HTML dialog spec](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLDialogElement/showModal) where the focus trap involves setting outside elements inert.

keyProps.name: unmountOnClose
keyProps.description: Decides whether the dialog should be removed from the DOM tree when it is closed. This can be useful when dealing with components that may contain state that should not be reset when the dialog is closed.

components.a11y: Manages focus trapping and aria-modal. Compose DialogTrigger/DialogSurface/DialogBody/DialogTitle/DialogActions. modalType controls dismiss behavior.

do: Dialog boxes consist of a header (`DialogTitle`), content (`DialogContent`), and footer (`DialogActions`), which should all be included inside a body (`DialogBody`).
Validate that people’s entries are acceptable before closing the dialog. Show an inline validation error near the field they must correct.

Modal dialogs should be used very sparingly—only when it’s critical that people make a choice or provide information before they can proceed. These dialogs are generally used for irreversible or potentially destructive tasks. They’re typically paired with a backdrop without a light dismiss.
Add a `aria-describedby` attribute on `DialogSurface` pointing to the dialog content on short confirmation like dialogs.
Add a `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` attribute on `DialogSurface` if there is no `DialogTitle`
dont: Don't use more than three buttons between `DialogActions`.

Don't open nested `Dialog`s. They are an anti-pattern and should be avoided. Nested dialogs create complex focus restoration logic and confuse users. If your design requires stacking dialogs, consider using a multi-step wizard within a single dialog, sequential dialogs, or a different UI component (panels, sidebars, popovers).
Don't use a `Dialog` with no focusable elements

<Dialog>
  <DialogTrigger disableButtonEnhancement>
    <Button>Open dialog</Button>
  </DialogTrigger>
  <DialogSurface>
    <DialogBody>
      <DialogTitle>Dialog title</DialogTitle>
      <DialogContent>
        Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipisicing elit. Quisquam
        exercitationem cumque repellendus eaque est dolor eius expedita
        nulla ullam? Tenetur reprehenderit aut voluptatum impedit voluptates
        in natus iure cumque eaque?
      </DialogContent>
      <DialogActions>
        <Button appearance="primary">Do Something</Button>

do: Provide a label for the Dropdown.

Set the Option's `value` prop if the content contains JSX. The Option value is used for keyboard accessibility to enable users to type a letter or string and jump to the matching option. The value is calculated from the children by default, but if the Option contains JSX, the `value` prop should be used to directly provide a string value.

Consider using `Dropdown` with outline or underline appearances. When the contrast ratio against the immediate surrounding color is less than 3:1, consider using underline or outline styles which has a bottom border stroke. But please ensure the color of bottom border stroke has a sufficient contrast which is greater than 3 to 1 against the immediate surrounding color.

keyProps.description: Current value of the input. Provide this if the input is a controlled component where you are maintaining its current state; otherwise, use `defaultValue`. (This prop is mutually exclusive with `defaultValue`.)

keyProps.description: An input can have different text-based [types](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/Input#input_types) based on the type of value the user will enter. Note that no custom styling is currently applied for alternative types, and some types may activate browser-default styling which does not match the Fluent design language. (For non-text-based types such as `button` or `checkbox`, use the appropriate component or an `<input>` element instead.)

components.a11y: Always associate a Label (via Field or htmlFor/id). Supports contentBefore/contentAfter slots for icons or units.

do: Consider using `Input` with underline or outline appearances. When the contrast ratio against the immediate surrounding color is less than 3:1, consider using underline or outline styles which has a bottom border stroke. But please ensure the color of bottom border stroke has a sufficient contrast which is greater than 3 to 1 against the immediate surrounding.
dont: Don't place input on a surface which doesn't have a sufficient contrast. The colors adjacent to the input should have a sufficient contrast. components.name: List
components.description: The List is a component for rendering set of vertically stacked items (other layouts are being discussed). These items can be focusable, selectable, have one primary action and one or more secondary actions.
components.a11y: Renders a <ul> by default. With no focusable children a List uses the list role; when selection is enabled it applies the listbox role to the root and option to each ListItem (grid is intentionally not used, to avoid empty cells). Use Left Arrow or Esc to return focus from a list item's actions to the parent container.

do: Use `tabIndex={0}` property on the `List` where the items have no actionable elements inside.
Use `navigationMode="items"` property on the `ListItem` when the list items should be focusable.
Use `navigationMode="composite"` property on the `ListItem` when the list items should be and there are other focusable elements inside of them.
use `onAction` callback to register primary action (click or `Enter` key)
Use `aria-label` property on the `ListItem` for custom screen reader label.
Rely on default accessibility roles, which are switched based on the `navigationMode` prop.
When `navigationMode` is `composite`, wrap each interactive item in `ListItem` in its own element with `role="gridcell"`.
dont: Don't use `tabIndex` on the `ListItem`, use `navigationMode` to get proper accessibility and keyboard navigation.
Don't use `navigationMode` on the `ListItem` if the list items have zero actionable elements, use `tabIndex={0}` on the `List` instead.
Don't use `onClick` for the list action, use `onAction` instead which adds automatic support for `Enter` and `Spacebar` keys

Use the `hasIcons` prop for alignment if only some menu items have icons.
Use the `hasCheckmarks` prop for alignment if only some menu items are selectable.
Use `MenuItemLink` if the menu item should navigate to a new page

Use `positioning={{ autoSize: true }}` if the Menu could potentially be clipped by the top of the page when forced to render above the trigger, or render past the bottom of the page when forced to render below the trigger (these can happen at high zoom or on small devices). Don't use more than 2 levels of nested menus.
Don't use verbose secondary content for menuitems.
Don't mix checkboxes and radio items without `MenuGroup`.

components.description: SpinButtons are used to allow numerical and non-numerical input bounded between minimum and maximum values with buttons to increment and decrement the input value. Values can also be manipulated via the keyboard.

keyProps.name: root
keyProps.description: The root element of SpinButton is a container `<div>`. The root slot receives the `className` and `style` specified on the `<SpinButton>`. All other native props are applied to the primary slot: `input`.

keyProps.name: input
keyProps.description: Input that displays the current value and accepts direct input from the user. Displayed value is formatted. This is the primary slot.

keyProps.name: incrementButton
keyProps.description: Renders the increment control.

keyProps.name: decrementButton
keyProps.description: Renders the decrement control.

keyProps.name: appearance
keyProps.description: Controls the colors and borders of the input.

keyProps.name: defaultValue
keyProps.description: Initial value of the control (assumed to be valid). Updates to this prop will not be respected. Use this if you intend for the SpinButton to be an uncontrolled component which maintains its own value. For a controlled component, use `value` instead. (Mutually exclusive with `value`.) Use `null` to indicate the control has no value.

keyProps.name: displayValue
keyProps.description: String representation of `value`. Use this when displaying the value to users as something other than a plain number. For example, when displaying currency values this might be "$1.00" when value is `1`. Only provide this if the SpinButton is a controlled component where you are maintaining its current state and passing updates based on change events. When SpinButton is used as an uncontrolled component this prop is ignored.

keyProps.name: onChange
keyProps.description: Callback for when the committed value changes. - User presses the up/down buttons (on single press or every spin) - User presses the up/down arrow keys (on single press or every spin) - User *commits* edits to the input text by focusing away (blurring) or pressing enter. Note that this is NOT called for every key press while the user is editing.

keyProps.name: precision
keyProps.description: How many decimal places the value should be rounded to. The default is calculated based on the precision of `step`: i.e. if step = 1, precision = 0. step = 0.0089, precision = 4. step = 300, precision = 2. step = 23.00, precision = 2.

keyProps.name: size
keyProps.description: Size of the input.

keyProps.name: stepPage
keyProps.description: Large difference between two values. This should be greater than `step` and is used when users hit the Page Up or Page Down keys.

keyProps.name: value
keyProps.description: Current value of the control (assumed to be valid). Only provide this if the SpinButton is a controlled component where you are maintaining its current state and passing updates based on change events; otherwise, use the `defaultValue` property. Use `null` to indicate the control has no value. Mutually exclusive with `defaultValue`.

components.a11y: Implements role="spinbutton"; arrow keys and Page Up/Down change the value. Provide a Label via Field.

do: Consider using `SpinButton` with underline or outline appearances. When the contrast ratio against the immediate surrounding color is less than 3:1, consider using underline or outline styles which has a bottom border stroke. But please ensure the color of bottom border stroke has a sufficient contrast which is greater than 3 to 1 against the immediate surrounding.
dont: Don’t place `SpinButton` on a surface which doesn’t have a sufficient contrast. The colors adjacent to the input should have a sufficient contrast. Particularly, the color of input with filled darker and lighter styles needs to provide greater than 3 to 1 contrast ratio against the immediate surrounding color to pass accessibility requirements.

components.a11y: Implements the ARIA tree pattern. Use FlatTree for large or virtualized data sets to keep the DOM flat.

do: Do use the `Tree` component to create a nested tree structure: When your data naturally follows a hierarchical parent-child relationship, the `Tree` component provides a clean and intuitive way to represent this structure. If a more complex interaction with a `Tree` is required, use `FlatTree` component instead: In scenarios where you need to efficiently manipulate or handle large amounts of hierarchical data, the `FlatTree` component can offer performance benefits.

Use custom styles if the tree needs to support more than 10 levels of nesting: Depending on your design and data requirements, you may need to adjust the styling of the tree elements to accommodate deeper nesting levels. See [inline styling tree item level](#inline-styling-tree-item-level) for more information.

Use the `aria-label` attribute on the root of the `Tree` component to provide an accessible name for the tree: This attribute helps screen readers to understand the purpose of the tree, making it more accessible and inclusive.

Ensure continuity of keyboard navigation when manipulating tree items: When adding or removing items, take necessary measures to prevent unexpected focus loss. The user's active focus should remain logical and intuitive throughout interactions.
If you provide additional functionality within tree items `actions` slot, make them accessible with a context menu:
Make `actions` or additional functionality in tree items accessible with a context menu:

Use `aria-selected=true` once a treeitem is selected in custom behaviors Some tree utilization might use the selection feature for navigation purposes, in this case, the `aria-selected` attribute should be set to `true` once the treeitem is the current active item to indicate that it is selected for the navigation.

  <TreeItem itemType="branch">
    <TreeItemLayout>level 1, item 1</TreeItemLayout>
    <Tree>
      <TreeItem itemType="leaf">
        <TreeItemLayout>level 2, item 1</TreeItemLayout>
      </TreeItem>
      <TreeItem itemType="leaf">
        <TreeItemLayout>level 2, item 2</TreeItemLayout>
      </TreeItem>
      <TreeItem itemType="leaf">
        <TreeItemLayout>level 2, item 3</TreeItemLayout>

    </Tree>

    <Tree>

        <TreeItemLayout>level 2, item 1</TreeItemLayout>
        <Tree>
          <TreeItem itemType="leaf">
            <TreeItemLayout>level 3, item 1</TreeItemLayout>
          </TreeItem>
        </Tree>
      </TreeItem>
    </Tree>
  </TreeItem>
  <TreeItem itemType="leaf">

  </TreeItem>

components.name: MenuGrid
components.description: A menu grid displays a complex menu structured as grid with sub-actions. It is usually rendered inside of the `Menu` component.

keyProps.name: circular
keyProps.description: Whether keyboard navigation wraps from the last row to the first and vice versa.

do: Use `MenuTrigger` as the first child of `Menu`.
Use `MenuGrid` as the only child of `MenuPopover`.
Use `MenuGridItem` instead of the `MenuGridRow` and `MenuGridCell` components when possible because `MenuGridItem` with its slots creates the proper grid structure for you.

Use `{ visuallyHidden: true }` for the `firstSubAction` or `secondSubAction` slots of `MenuGridItem` if you want to omit a sub-action for certain menu grid items making the sub-actions asymmetric. This is necessary to maintain the proper grid structure.
Use small transparent buttons inside of the cells for best layout.
Use the `aria-label` attribute on `MenuGridItem` or `MenuGridRow` to set a proper row name which will be narrated for screen reader users when navigating in menu grid using the Down or Up arrow keys.
dont: Don't use the `MenuGridItem` or `MenuGridRow` components as children of `MenuList`. They are only intended to work within `MenuGrid`.

Don't place more than one actionable element to the `firstSubAction` or `secondSubAction` slot. If you need to provide more than two actionable elements for a menu grid item, use the `MenuGridRow` and `MenuGridCell` compound components and place each actionable element into its own `MenuGridCell` as instructed in the story below. Alternatively, consider creating a menu button as a submenu using one of the sub-action slots as also instructed in the story below and place your actions into the submenu.
Don't make `MenuGridCell` components, `firstSubAction` and `secondSubAction` slots focusable using the `tabIndex` attribute with value `0` if they are empty or `visuallyHidden`, respectively.

  <MenuTrigger disableButtonEnhancement>

  </MenuTrigger>
  <MenuPopover>
    <MenuGrid>
      {items.map((name) => (
        <MenuGridItem
          key={name}
          onClick={() => showAlert(name)}
          aria-label={name}
          icon={
            <Button
              size="small"
              appearance="transparent"
              icon={<GlobePersonRegular />}
              aria-label={`Profile card for ${name}`}
            />
          }
          firstSubAction={
            <Button
              size="small"
              appearance="transparent"
              icon={<DeleteRegular />}
              aria-label={`Remove ${name}`}
            />
          }
        >
          {name}
        </MenuGridItem>
      ))}
    </MenuGrid>
  </MenuPopover>
</Menu>

components.description: `createMotionComponent()` is a factory function that creates a custom motion component powered by Web Animations API.

keyProps.name: imperativeRef
keyProps.description: Provides imperative controls for the animation.

keyProps.name: onMotionFinish
keyProps.description: Callback that is called when the whole motion finishes. A motion definition can contain multiple animations and therefore multiple "finish" events. The callback is triggered once all animations have finished with "null" instead of an event object to avoid ambiguity.

keyProps.name: onMotionCancel
keyProps.description: Callback that is called when the whole motion is cancelled. A motion definition can contain multiple animations and therefore multiple "cancel" events. The callback is triggered once all animations have been cancelled with "null" instead of an event object to avoid ambiguity.

keyProps.name: onMotionStart
keyProps.description: Callback that is called when the whole motion starts. A motion definition can contain multiple animations and therefore multiple "start" events. The callback is triggered when the first animation is started. There is no official "start" event with the Web Animations API. so the callback is triggered with "null".

keyProps.name: replayKey
keyProps.description:
When this value changes, the animation replays from the start on the same DOM element, cancelling any in-progress animation, without remounting the component or its children. **Why not just use a React `key`?** Changing a React `key` forces a full unmount and remount of the subtree: DOM nodes are destroyed and recreated, focus is lost, and any child state is reset. `replayKey` avoids all of that — only the animation effect reruns while the DOM and component state remain intact. Use this when you want to retrigger a motion in response to a state change (e.g. a user action or a data update) while preserving DOM continuity. It is the declarative equivalent of calling `imperativeRef.current.play()` but driven by a prop rather than a ref call. @example ```tsx // Replay a Fade.In each time the user clicks "Refresh" const [replayKey, setReplayKey] = React.useState(0);

 ```

keyProps.description: Provides imperative controls for the animation.

keyProps.name: onMotionFinish
keyProps.description: Callback that is called when the whole motion finishes. A motion definition can contain multiple animations and therefore multiple "finish" events. The callback is triggered once all animations have finished with "null" instead of an event object to avoid ambiguity.

keyProps.name: onMotionCancel
keyProps.description: Callback that is called when the whole motion is cancelled. When a motion is cancelled it does not emit a finish event but a specific cancel event A motion definition can contain multiple animations and therefore multiple "finish" events. The callback is triggered once all animations have finished with "null" instead of an event object to avoid ambiguity.

keyProps.name: onMotionStart
keyProps.description: Callback that is called when the whole motion starts. A motion definition can contain multiple animations and therefore multiple "start" events. The callback is triggered when the first animation is started. There is no official "start" event with the Web Animations API. so the callback is triggered with "null".

components.name: AriaLiveAnnouncer
components.description: `AriaLiveAnnouncer` provides a sample implementation of an `aria-live` region that can be used to announce messages to screen readers.
components.reactImport: import { AriaLiveAnnouncer, Button, Field, Input, useAnnounce } from '@fluentui/react-components';

components.name: useAnnounce
components.description: `useAnnounce()` is a React hook that provides a function that can be used to announce messages to screen readers.
components.reactImport: import { Button, Field, Input, Radio, RadioGroup, useAnnounce } from '@fluentui/react-components';
components.sample:
<Field label="A message for annoucement">
  <Input
    onChange={(ev, data) => setMessage(data.value)}
    value={message}
  />
</Field>
<Field label="Message type">
  <RadioGroup
    onChange={(ev, data) =>
      setMessageType(data.value as "polite" | "assertive")
    }
    value={messageType}
  >
    <Radio label="assertive" value="assertive" />
    <Radio label="polite" value="polite" />
  </RadioGroup>
</Field>

<Button
  onClick={() => {
    announce(message, {
      polite: messageType === "polite",
    });
  }}
>
  Announce message
</Button>

components.name: useTypingAnnounce
components.description: `useTypingAnnounce` takes a reference to an element (which should be an `input`, `textarea`, or `contenteditable`) and returns a ref to put on the editable input element and a `typingAnnounce` function with the same paramters as the `announce` function returned by `useAnnounce`.

components.sample:
<AriaLiveAnnouncer>
  <Field
    label="A field with a maxlength of 20"
    validationState={overLimit ? "error" : undefined}
  >
    <Input onChange={onChange} ref={inputRef} />
  </Field>
</AriaLiveAnnouncer>

components.name: ActionButtonShim
components.description: The ActionButtonShim component accepts the same props as a v8 ActionButton and renders a v9 Button.

keyProps.name: componentRef
keyProps.description: Optional callback to access the `IButton` interface. Use this instead of `ref` for accessing the public methods and properties of the component.

keyProps.name: elementRef
keyProps.description: Optional callback to access the root DOM element.
keyProps.deprecated: Temporary solution which will be replaced with ref in the V8 release.

keyProps.name: href
keyProps.description: If provided, this component will be rendered as an anchor. @defaultvalue ElementType.anchor

keyProps.name: primary
keyProps.description: Changes the visual presentation of the button to be emphasized. @defaultvalue false

keyProps.name: uniqueId
keyProps.description: Unique ID to identify the item. Typically a duplicate of key value.

keyProps.name: disabled
keyProps.description: Whether the button is disabled

keyProps.name: allowDisabledFocus
keyProps.description: Whether the button can have focus in disabled mode

keyProps.name: primaryDisabled
keyProps.description: If set to true and this is a split button (`split` is true), the split button's primary action is disabled.

keyProps.name: styles
keyProps.description: Custom styling for individual elements within the button DOM.

keyProps.name: theme
keyProps.description: Theme provided by HOC.

keyProps.name: checked
keyProps.description: Whether the button is checked. Should be used with the `toggle` attribute when creating a standalone on/off button.

keyProps.name: toggle
keyProps.description: Whether button is a toggle button with distinct on and off states. This should be true for buttons that permanently change state when a press event finishes, such as a volume mute button.

keyProps.name: className
keyProps.description: If provided, additional class name to provide on the root element.

keyProps.name: ariaLabel
keyProps.description: The aria label of the button for the benefit of screen readers.

keyProps.name: ariaDescription
keyProps.description: Detailed description of the button for the benefit of screen readers. Besides the compound button, other button types will need more information provided to screen reader.

keyProps.name: ariaHidden
keyProps.description: If true, add an `aria-hidden` attribute instructing screen readers to ignore the element.

keyProps.name: text
keyProps.description: Text to render button label. If text is supplied, it will override any string in button children. Other children components will be passed through after the text.

keyProps.name: iconProps
keyProps.description: The props for the icon shown in the button.

keyProps.name: menuProps
keyProps.description: Props for button menu. Providing this will default to showing the menu icon. See `menuIconProps` for overriding how the default icon looks. Providing this in addition to `onClick` and setting the `split` property to `true` will render a SplitButton.

keyProps.name: onAfterMenuDismiss
keyProps.description: Callback that runs after Button's contextual menu was closed (removed from the DOM)

keyProps.name: split
keyProps.description: If set to true, and if `menuProps` and `onClick` are provided, the button will render as a SplitButton.

keyProps.name: menuIconProps
keyProps.description: The props for the icon shown when providing a menu dropdown.

keyProps.name: splitButtonAriaLabel
keyProps.description: Accessible label for the dropdown chevron button if this button is split.

keyProps.name: onMenuClick
keyProps.type: ((ev?: KeyboardEvent<HTMLElement> | MouseEvent<HTMLElement, MouseEvent>, button?: IButtonProps) => void) | undefined
keyProps.description: Optional callback when menu is clicked.

keyProps.name: onRenderIcon
keyProps.description: Custom render function for the icon

keyProps.name: onRenderText
keyProps.description: Custom render function for the label text.

keyProps.name: onRenderDescription
keyProps.description: Custom render function for the description text.

keyProps.name: onRenderAriaDescription
keyProps.description: Custom render function for the aria description element.

keyProps.name: onRenderChildren
keyProps.description: Custom render function for rendering the button children.

keyProps.name: onRenderMenuIcon
keyProps.description: Custom render function for button menu icon

keyProps.name: onRenderMenu
keyProps.deprecated: Deprecated at v6.3.2, to be removed at \>= v7.0.0. Use `menuAs` instead.

keyProps.name: menuAs
keyProps.description: Render a custom menu in place of the normal one.

keyProps.name: secondaryText
keyProps.description: Description of the action this button takes. Only used for compound buttons.

keyProps.name: buttonType
keyProps.description: @defaultvalue ButtonType.default
keyProps.deprecated: Deprecated at v1.2.3, to be removed at \>= v2.0.0. Use specific button component instead.

keyProps.name: rootProps
keyProps.deprecated: Deprecated at v0.56.2, to be removed at \>= v1.0.0. Use native props on the Button itself instead. They will be mixed into the button/anchor element rendered by the component.

keyProps.name: toggled
keyProps.deprecated: No longer used. Use `checked` if setting state.

keyProps.name: data
keyProps.description: Any custom data the developer wishes to associate with the button.

keyProps.name: getClassNames
keyProps.type: ((theme: ITheme, className: string, variantClassName: string, iconClassName: string, menuIconClassName: string, disabled: boolean, checked: boolean, expanded: boolean, hasMenu: boolean, isSplit: boolean | undefined, allowDisabledFocus: boolean) => IButtonClas…
keyProps.description: Method to provide the classnames to style a button. The default value for this prop is the `getClassnames` func defined in `BaseButton.classnames.ts`. @defaultvalue getBaseButtonClassNames

keyProps.name: getSplitButtonClassNames
keyProps.type: ((disabled: boolean, expanded: boolean, checked: boolean, allowDisabledFocus: boolean) => ISplitButtonClassNames)
keyProps.description: Method to provide the classnames to style a button. The default value for this prop is the `getClassnames` func defined in `BaseButton.classnames.ts`. @defaultvalue getBaseSplitButtonClassNames

keyProps.name: menuTriggerKeyCode
keyProps.description: Provides a custom KeyCode that can be used to open the button menu. A value of `null` can be provided to disable opening the button menu with a key press.

keyProps.name: keytipProps
keyProps.description: Optional keytip for this button

keyProps.name: persistMenu
keyProps.description: Menu will not be created or destroyed when opened or closed, instead it will be hidden. This will improve perf of the menu opening but could potentially impact overall perf by having more elements in the dom. Should only be used when menu perf is important. Note: This may increase the amount of time it takes for the button itself to mount.

keyProps.name: renderPersistedMenuHiddenOnMount
keyProps.description: If true, the persisted menu is rendered hidden when the button initially mounts. Non-persisted menus will not be in the component tree unless they are being shown. Note: This increases the time the button will take to mount, but can improve perceived menu open perf. when the user opens the menu. @defaultvalue `undefined`, equivalent to false
keyProps.deprecated: There is known bug in Edge when this prop is true where scrollbars overlap with the content when a menu is first rendered hidden. Please do not start using this. If you are already using this, please make sure that you are doing so only in non-Edge browsers. See: https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui/issues/9034

keyProps.name: splitButtonMenuProps
keyProps.description: Experimental prop that get passed into the menuButton that's rendered as part of split button. Anything passed in will likely need to have accompanying style changes.

keyProps.name: description
keyProps.description: Style for the description text if applicable (for compound buttons).
keyProps.deprecated: Use `secondaryText` instead.

keyProps.name: defaultRender
keyProps.description: yet unknown docs

keyProps.name: primaryActionButtonProps
keyProps.description: Optional props to be applied only to the primary action button of SplitButton and not to the overall SplitButton container

components.description: The CheckboxShim component accepts the same props as a v8 Checkbox and renders a v9 Checkbox.

keyProps.name: componentRef
keyProps.description: Optional callback to access the `ICheckbox` interface. Use this instead of `ref` for accessing the public methods and properties of the component.

keyProps.name: className
keyProps.description: Class name to provide on the root element, in addition to the `ms-Checkbox` class.

keyProps.name: checked
keyProps.description: Checked state. Mutually exclusive with `defaultChecked`. Use this if you control the checked state at a higher level and plan to pass in the correct value based on handling `onChange` events and re-rendering.

keyProps.name: defaultChecked
keyProps.description: Default checked state. Mutually exclusive with `checked`. Use this if you want an uncontrolled component, meaning the Checkbox instance maintains its own state.

keyProps.name: label
keyProps.description: Label to display next to the checkbox.

keyProps.name: disabled
keyProps.description: Disabled state of the checkbox.

keyProps.name: required
keyProps.description: Required state of the checkbox.

keyProps.name: onChange
keyProps.type: ((ev?: FormEvent<HTMLElement | HTMLInputElement>, checked?: boolean) => void) | undefined
keyProps.description: Callback that is called when the checked value has changed.

keyProps.name: title
keyProps.description: Title text applied to the root element and the hidden checkbox input. (Use `label` instead for the visible label.)

keyProps.name: id
keyProps.description: ID for the checkbox input.

keyProps.name: name
keyProps.description: Name for the checkbox input. This is intended for use with forms and NOT displayed in the UI.

keyProps.name: inputProps
keyProps.description: Optional props that will be applied to the input element, *before* other props are applied. Note that if you provide, for example, `disabled` as well as `inputProps.disabled`, the top-level prop (`disabled` in this case) will take precedence. Including `data-*` props in `inputProps` is supported but currently requires casting since TS 3.7 doesn't provide a way to allow all keys with a certain prefix.

keyProps.name: boxSide
keyProps.description: Determines whether the checkbox should be shown before the label (`start`) or after (`end`). @defaultvalue 'start'

keyProps.name: theme
keyProps.description: Theme provided by HOC.

keyProps.name: ariaLabel
keyProps.description: Accessible label for the checkbox.

keyProps.name: ariaLabelledBy
keyProps.description: ID for element that contains label information for the checkbox.

keyProps.name: ariaDescribedBy
keyProps.description: ID for element that provides extended information for the checkbox.

keyProps.name: ariaPositionInSet
keyProps.description: The position in the parent set (if in a set) for `aria-posinset`.

keyProps.name: ariaSetSize
keyProps.description: The total size of the parent set (if in a set) for `aria-setsize`.

keyProps.name: styles
keyProps.description: Call to provide customized styling that will layer on top of the variant rules.

keyProps.name: onRenderLabel
keyProps.description: Custom render function for the label.

keyProps.name: checkmarkIconProps
keyProps.description: Custom icon props for the check mark rendered by the checkbox

keyProps.name: indeterminate
keyProps.description: Optional controlled indeterminate visual state for checkbox. Setting indeterminate state takes visual precedence over `checked` or `defaultChecked` props given but does not affect checked state. This should not be a toggleable state. On load, the checkbox will receive indeterminate visual state. After the first user click, your supplied `onChange` callback should remove the indeterminate state (without modifying the checked state), exposing the true state of the checkbox.

components.name: StackShim
components.description: The StackShim and StackItemShim accept the same props a v8 Stack and StackItem and render equivalent HTML and stylings to provide layout using CSS flexbox.
components.reactImport:
import { Checkbox, Stack } from '@fluentui/react';
import { StackItemShim, StackShim } from '@fluentui/react-migration-v8-v9';

keyProps.name: as
keyProps.description: Defines how to render the Stack.

keyProps.name: horizontal
keyProps.description: Defines whether to render Stack children horizontally. @defaultvalue false

keyProps.name: reversed
keyProps.description: Defines whether to render Stack children in the opposite direction (bottom-to-top if it's a vertical Stack and right-to-left if it's a horizontal Stack). @defaultvalue false

keyProps.name: horizontalAlign
keyProps.description: Defines how to align Stack children horizontally (along the x-axis).

keyProps.name: verticalAlign
keyProps.description: Defines how to align Stack children vertically (along the y-axis).

keyProps.name: verticalFill
keyProps.description: Defines whether the Stack should take up 100% of the height of its parent. This property is required to be set to true when using the `grow` flag on children in vertical oriented Stacks. Stacks are rendered as block elements and grow horizontally to the container already. @defaultvalue false

keyProps.name: disableShrink
keyProps.description: Defines whether Stack children should not shrink to fit the available space. @defaultvalue false

keyProps.name: grow
keyProps.description: Defines how much to grow the Stack in proportion to its siblings.

keyProps.name: gap
keyProps.description: Defines the spacing between Stack children. The property is specified as a value for 'row gap', followed optionally by a value for 'column gap'. If 'column gap' is omitted, it's set to the same value as 'row gap'.
keyProps.deprecated: Use `tokens.childrenGap` instead.

keyProps.name: maxWidth
keyProps.description: Defines the maximum width that the Stack can take.
keyProps.deprecated: Use `tokens.maxWidth` instead.

keyProps.name: maxHeight
keyProps.description: Defines the maximum height that the Stack can take.
keyProps.deprecated: Use `tokens.maxHeight` instead.

keyProps.name: padding
keyProps.description: Defines the inner padding of the Stack.
keyProps.deprecated: Use `tokens.padding` instead.

keyProps.name: wrap
keyProps.description: Defines whether Stack children should wrap onto multiple rows or columns when they are about to overflow the size of the Stack. @defaultvalue false

keyProps.name: enableScopedSelectors
keyProps.description: Defines if scoped style selectors are enabled for the Stack component, which greatly helps in style recalculation performance, but requires children of the Stack to be able to accept a className prop (excluding Fragments). @defaultvalue false

keyProps.name: doNotRenderFalsyValues
keyProps.description: When receiving a falsy value, render null instead.
keyProps.deprecated: Default behavior now allows rendering falsy values so cases like this one can happen: ```tsx <Stack>0 1 2 3 4</Stack> ```

keyProps.name: root
keyProps.description: Defines root slot of the component.

keyProps.name: inner
keyProps.description: Defines a slot that is placed inside the root slot in order to achieve wrapping. Only used when the wrap property is set to true.

<StackShim
  as={"span"}
  verticalFill={state.verticalFill}
  horizontal={state.horizontal}
  reversed={state.reversed}
  wrap={state.wrap}
  disableShrink={state.disableShrink}
  horizontalAlign={state.horizontalAlign}
  verticalAlign={state.verticalAlign}
  tokens={{
    childrenGap: childrenGapToken,
    padding: paddingToken,
    maxHeight: "500px",
    maxWidth: "500px",
  }}
  className={stackShimStyles}
>
  <StackItemShim className={stackItemShimStyles}>
    Stack Item{" "}
  </StackItemShim>
  <StackItemShim align={"end"} className={stackItemShimStyles}>
    Stack Item Self Aligned
  </StackItemShim>
  <StackItemShim grow={1} className={stackItemShimStyles}>
    Stack Item Grow
  </StackItemShim>

  <Checkbox label="checkbox 2" className={stackItemShimStyles} />
</StackShim>

components.name: ChatInput
components.description: The rich chat composer: a multiline editor with a send action, optional character count/limit, attachments and expand/collapse behavior. onSubmit fires with { value: string }.
components.a11y: Provide an aria-label (there is no placeholder prop; the editor is contentEditable). ChatInputProps is a discriminated union: charactersRemainingMessage is required (a (remaining:number)=>string callback with maxLength, or undefined without). onSubmit fires on Enter/Send; onStop cancels an in-flight response while isSending.

<ChatInput
  aria-label="Ask Copilot"
  maxLength={2000}
  charactersRemainingMessage={(remaining) => `${remaining} characters remaining`}
  showCount
  onSubmit={(_, data) => sendMessage(data.value)}
/>

siteGuidance.name: Chat input
siteGuidance.description: The chat input is the area in a Copilot chat where a user can enter their Copilot prompt or question. It’s aimed more at conversational UX than durable content generation. If you need a component to help people create entities, try the Prompt input. Composed input surface: the primary component is ChatInput (a rich, contentEditable Lexical composer) wired to a SendButton, with optional attachments, character count and an expand/collapse ExpandButton.
siteGuidance.a11y: No placeholder prop (the editor is contentEditable) — label it with aria-label. ChatInputProps is a discriminated union: charactersRemainingMessage is required (a (remaining:number)=>string callback with maxLength, or undefined without). onSubmit fires on Enter/Send; onStop cancels an in-flight response while isSending.
siteGuidance.sample:
<ChatInput
  aria-label="Ask Copilot"
  maxLength={2000}
  charactersRemainingMessage={(remaining) => `${remaining} characters remaining`}
  showCount
  onSubmit={(_, data) => sendMessage(data.value)}
/>

siteGuidance.name: Citations and references
siteGuidance.description: Citations and references help build trust for AI experiences by surfacing the information Copilot used to create its output. References represent the source grounding data. Citations connect a Copilot output to a reference. A cluster: Citation is the inline marker that connects an answer to a source; Reference is the grounding chip (slot-based: root, citation, divider, content, graphic + designVersion); ReferenceList lays out references with overflow. keyProps below are annotated with their owning component.
siteGuidance.a11y: Give each Citation/Reference an accessible label describing the cited source. useReferenceCitationPreview / generateReferenceCitationPreview wire a Citation–Reference pair with matching preview surfaces.

</ReferenceList>

This is a composed pattern with no single scalar-prop component: CopilotChat is a slot-only scrollable container that lays out UserMessage / CopilotMessage / SystemMessage (plus Timestamp, AiGeneratedDisclaimer and a ScrollDownButton). See those component entries for props.
siteGuidance.a11y: CopilotChat renders the message-list region; place UserMessage/CopilotMessage/SystemMessage children inside and pair with ScrollDownButton for long conversations. Props live on the child message components, not on CopilotChat.
siteGuidance.note: Composed pattern: props live on the composing components listed in apiComponents.

components.name: GhostText

siteGuidance.name: Prompt starters
siteGuidance.description: Prompt starters give people hints about how they can interact with Copilot. Use them to teach how to build prompts, give users a starting point for building a robust prompt, and show Copilot capabilities. Prompt starters are most often found in zero prompt experiences or inside the prompt library dialog. PromptStarterList is the container (grid + show more/less); each item is a PromptStarterV2 (slots: icon, category, prompt, reasonMarker, actions). PromptStarter (the v1 item) is deprecated (10/21/2025) — use PromptStarterV2. keyProps below are PromptStarterList props.
siteGuidance.a11y: PromptStarterList uses arrow-key navigation (customizable via arrowNavigationOptions). Label the expand/collapse button with expandButtonLabel / collapseButtonLabel.

components.name: Icon
components.description: Fluent 2 icons ship as individual React components (Regular and Filled variants per icon, at several sizes) from @fluentui/react-icons. There is no generic <Icon> component - import the icon you need, or pair a Regular/Filled couple with bundleIcon.

keyProps.name: className
keyProps.description: Style the icon with makeStyles; size and color follow font-size and color.

keyProps.name: primaryFill
keyProps.description: Overrides the fill; prefer inheriting currentColor so the icon follows the theme.

keyProps.name: aria-label
keyProps.description: Required when the icon is the only content of an interactive element.

keyProps.name: aria-hidden
keyProps.description: Set on decorative icons that sit next to a visible label.

components.a11y: Icons are decorative by default and inherit the text color (currentColor via primaryFill). For a purely decorative icon add aria-hidden or render it inside an already-labeled control; for a meaningful standalone icon give it an accessible name via the title prop or a wrapping element's aria-label. Never rely on color alone to convey meaning.
components.sample:
const Add = bundleIcon(AddFilled, AddRegular);

<Add aria-hidden />
